title: The integrated addressing/execution/verification boundary, gated by an eight-criterion representability gate before the task population
question: When the retained candidate set is reduced from H to K before structural execution, does an acceptable candidate survive addressing, does CASM-S then compute the target relation on it, and does an independent verifier confirm it — measured as four stage-separated endpoints behind a representability gate that checks the instrument before the task population runs?
hypothesis: For the controlled multi-valid equality benchmark, exact addressing retains an acceptable candidate with probability near its analytic ceiling while executing at most K structures per query. The successor hypothesis to C5-002's is that the instrument failure was a specification error in the bridge's training target — trained on single candidates against their Boolean output, it optimised absolute accuracy while the downstream decision is a within-query separation — so a bridge trained on pairs against a margin objective separates satisfier from violator at or above the registered minimum, and a gate with eight pre-registered criteria then admits the instrument before the task population runs. The four stage endpoints remain separated as in C5-002: coverage_rate reads no CASM-S output, so an execution failure cannot depress an addressing number.

arms.name: exhaustive
arms.intervention: execute every H candidate structure through the CASM-S evaluator, with addressing evaluated separately as the trivial retention of the full set

arms.name: exact-indexed
arms.intervention: content-address the candidate universe and execute only the retained K candidates, with the bucket compared against the acceptable set for the addressing endpoint

arms.name: representation-addressed
arms.intervention: retain candidates by fixed cosine similarity of public query bits and candidate descriptors, evaluated by the same addressing endpoint

endpoints.name: coverage_rate
endpoints.role: primary — the (S,Q) to R stage: an acceptable candidate is retained
endpoints.description: Fraction of measured queries where the retained set intersects the hidden acceptable-action set. Computed from the retained indices and the hidden acceptable set alone; no CASM-S output, selection result or verification result enters it, so an execution failure cannot depress an addressing number. This is C5-002's separation contract, carried forward unchanged.

endpoints.name: execution_accuracy_rate
endpoints.role: secondary — the (R,Q) to A stage: the relation is computed correctly on a retained candidate
endpoints.description: Fraction of measured queries where the relation holds on a selected retained candidate. The acceptable set is hidden from the executor; the endpoint reads only the public relation, the selected candidate's descriptor and the executed output.

endpoints.name: verification_rate
endpoints.role: secondary — the (A,O) to V stage: an independent verifier confirms the computation
endpoints.description: Fraction of measured queries where RelationConstraintVerifier agrees that the executed output matches the public relation. The verifier reads the computation's trace and the public relation only. Zero across all arms is the signature of an instrument failure rather than a negative result, which is why criterion 4 of the gate checks verifier acceptance on held-out structures before the population runs.

endpoints.name: structures_executed_per_query
endpoints.role: secondary — the R to W(R) stage: actual structural execution count
endpoints.description: Number of retained structures submitted to CASM-S per measured query. The work endpoints are counted from the actual serialized graph submitted to the external model, so they survive an instrument failure and are what carries the 128x observation forward.

endpoints.name: active_nodes_per_query
endpoints.description: Active CASM-S nodes across executed retained structures per query.

endpoints.name: candidate_edges_per_query
endpoints.description: Candidate edges presented to CASM-S across all executed retained structures per query.

endpoints.name: gate_evaluations_per_query
endpoints.description: Per-edge CASM-S gate evaluations across executed retained structures per query.

endpoints.name: structural_operations_per_query
endpoints.description: Non-input CASM-S node operations executed per query.

endpoints.name: node_outputs_per_query
endpoints.description: Active CASM-S node outputs produced per query.

endpoints.name: casm_forward_batches
endpoints.description: Number of batched CASM-S forward calls over the measured query window. One forward can carry several structures, so this is never read as a structure count.

endpoints.name: address_positions_per_query
endpoints.description: Candidate positions the content-address index inspects per query. This is the addressing arm's own work measure and is zero on arms that do not use the index — so it is what separates an addressing cost from an execution cost, which a single work total cannot show.

endpoints.name: representation_candidates_scored_per_query
endpoints.description: Candidates the fixed cosine scorer evaluates per query. Registered so the representation arm's addressing cost is visible as a cost rather than only as a coverage number, and so the arm cannot appear free.

endpoints.name: wall_clock_seconds
endpoints.description: Measured runtime of the C5 query window on the declared hardware. A diagnostic, never a capability endpoint.

endpoints.name: gate_accuracy
endpoints.role: secondary — the representability gate's own separation score
endpoints.description: Fraction of held-out pairs the frozen bridge separates under the registered threshold. Reported whether or not the gate passes, because a failed gate is the instrument's report rather than an absence of one. It is not a capability endpoint and cannot be cited as one.

decision_rule.condition: any of the eight pre-registered representability criteria fails on held-out structures
decision_rule.licenses: the run terminates as instrument-invalid and no C5 capability number is reported; the failure is recorded against the criterion that fired, not against CASM-S as a substrate
decision_rule.does_not_license: any capability claim or negative capability claim, including that selective execution cannot work or that CASM-S cannot execute the relation

decision_rule.condition: exact-indexed coverage_rate is at or above its analytic ceiling within the seed spread while structures_executed_per_query is no greater than K
decision_rule.licenses: the tested exact addressing boundary retains an acceptable candidate at the analytic ceiling for this controlled benchmark, and the measured CASM-S work follows the retained set
decision_rule.does_not_license: semantic retrieval, learned addressing, or the full system-level C5 claim

decision_rule.condition: exact-indexed coverage_rate is materially below its analytic ceiling at the same H and K
decision_rule.licenses: retention loss is observed under the tested retained-set budget and is attributable to addressing rather than to execution, because the endpoint reads no CASM-S output
decision_rule.does_not_license: that selective execution or cheap addressing is impossible

decision_rule.condition: execution_accuracy_rate is materially below the gate-confirmed representability reference while coverage_rate is at its ceiling
decision_rule.licenses: the failure is localized to the (R,Q) to A execution stage, and the coverage endpoint remains a valid addressing measurement
decision_rule.does_not_license: that addressing is the defect, or a general statement about CASM-S execution capability

decision_rule.condition: verification_rate is materially below execution_accuracy_rate while both gates passed
decision_rule.licenses: the (A,O) to V verification stage disagrees with the execution stage, which is a finding about the verifier or the trace rather than about CASM-S, and requires audit before a C5 interpretation
decision_rule.does_not_license: a statement about CASM-S capability, since the two stages read the same output under different criteria

decision_rule.condition: structures_executed_per_query or CASM work fails to decrease with the retained set under otherwise matched conditions
decision_rule.licenses: the implementation does not expose the intended structural work reduction and requires audit before a C5 interpretation
decision_rule.does_not_license: a general statement about CASM-S efficiency

held_constant: CASM-S source commit is pinned to c31554413301e3c9d3e6b3f8c8c6be572a74a748

the representability gate has eight registered criteria and runs before the task population; a failure of any one terminates the run as instrument-invalid, so no capability number is emitted under an unrepresentative instrument

criterion 4 is verifier acceptance on the satisfying half of each held-out pair, not over both halves: RelationConstraintVerifier is a success verifier and necessarily rejects a violating descriptor, so two-sided acceptance is capped at one half by construction (see amendment A2)
the gate evaluates held-out structures under the same ops, threshold, bridge calibration and execution path the task population uses, not a proxy task
the gate's seed stream is disjoint from the task population's seeds, so the gate cannot be calibrated on the evaluation population
the coverage endpoint reads only retained indices and the hidden acceptable set; no CASM-S output, selection result or verification result may enter it
the acceptable set is hidden from the executor and from addressing; it is revealed only after execution for evaluation

the bridge's training objective is pair_separation, registered as BRIDGE_OBJECTIVE: the loss is on the margin score(satisfying) minus score(violating) over pairs, not on the absolute level of either candidate's output

bridge calibration constants are unchanged from C5-002 except the objective and the validation stream's seed: 512 training examples, 128 validation, 100 epochs, lr 2e-3, training seed 20260929, validation seed 20261001 (see amendment A1)
the gate threshold is the verifier's own decision boundary: GATE_THRESHOLD = 0.5, and the minimum separation is GATE_MIN_ACCURACY = 0.5, both pre-registered before C5-002's run and unchanged after it
the transported CASM-S spec never carries true_edges, target, input_values, truth_table or acceptable_actions; runtime inputs are passed separately to the executor
no oracle information enters routing or execution; the forbidden field set is audited at the gate rather than assumed
the checkpoint sha256 is recorded in the run record and the run is deterministic from it; structure keys are formatted strings because hash() on strings is salted per process
same CASM-S model instance, checkpoint and evaluator are used across all arms
same candidate population and task stream are used for matched seed and H cells
candidate validity is multiple-valid on two marked equality positions
the exhaustive arm executes every candidate but must not use a CASM-S output to select for the coverage endpoint
the exact-indexed arm is the retention ceiling and analytic control, not a learned result
the representation-addressed arm is a fixed cosine baseline and is explicitly not a learned semantic-addressing result
no exhaustive fallback is permitted after an empty retained set
hidden target and acceptable_actions are used only after execution for evaluation
warmup queries are fixed at 3 and excluded from endpoint averages
CASM work is counted from the actual serialized graph submitted to the external model

amendments.applies_to: held_constant: the bridge-calibration line, and the validation stream's seed
amendments.old_definition: bridge calibration constants are unchanged from C5-002 in every respect except the objective: 512 training examples, 128 validation, 100 epochs, lr 2e-3, seed 20260929. The validation stream was drawn with BRIDGE_SEED + 1, which equals 20260930, the gate's own seed — the same stream read under two names
amendments.new_definition: the bridge's training stream seeds at BRIDGE_SEED = 20260929 and its validation stream at the named constant BRIDGE_VALIDATION_SEED = 20261001, and the gate at GATE_SEED = 20260930. Three named constants rather than one plus arithmetic, so the three streams' disjointness is visible as three values and is not inferred from an offset
amendments.rationale: C5-002 derived its validation seed as BRIDGE_SEED + 1, which is exactly GATE_SEED, so its reported validation separation and its gate verdict read the same structures under two names: the gate was checking a stream the calibration had already seen, and the two numbers were not independent observations of one quantity. The identity it produced was 'unchanged in every respect except the objective', which the validation seed did not hold, so the line as registered asserted a sameness the successor does not have. The defect is in C5-002's design and is carried forward silently unless recorded, and a successor that fixes it without an amendment is a successor whose calibration differs from the design it claims to repeat — which is precisely the confound the identity exists to prevent. Naming the seed removes the arithmetic that hid the collision and keeps the four calibration constants C5-002 named (512/128/100/2e-3 and the training seed) exactly as they were; only the validation stream's seed and the way it is specified change
amendments.discovered: by reading scripts/measure_c5_casm_002.py:256 against the C5-003 script's named constants, before any C5-003 confirmatory run. Not found by a run: the collision produces no anomaly in either script's own numbers, which is why it survived C5-002's run unremarked — both values are reported and neither is wrong on its own terms
amendments.affected: the bridge-calibration held_constant line, which now names two seeds and the exception; the validation stream's seed value; nothing else. The training seed, the example counts, the epoch count, the learning rate, the objective and the gate's own seed are all unchanged
amendments.no_result_under_previous_version: no confirmatory C5-003 run has been made. The only execution against this contract was a declared --smoke test, which exercises the script's contract check on a torch-free fake runtime and is recorded as smoke and not as a measurement; no number from it is evidence of anything about C5. C5-002's run is unaffected and stands as measured: its validation accuracy 0.84375 and its gate separation 0.2305 were computed on the same stream, and both remain what the run reported

amendments.applies_to: the gate's criterion 4, and the held_constant describing it
amendments.old_definition: actual verifier acceptance, measured as verification_acceptance over the same 512 held-out pairs, minimum GATE_MIN_ACCURACY, read as acceptance over both halves of every pair
amendments.new_definition: verifier acceptance on the satisfying half: the fraction of the 512 held-out pairs for which RelationConstraintVerifier.verify_task accepts the satisfying descriptor on the model's own output, with n_compared = the number of pairs and n_accepted the number accepted, minimum GATE_MIN_ACCURACY = 0.5. The violating half is not part of the score
amendments.rationale: RelationConstraintVerifier is a success verifier: on a descriptor the public relation does not hold for, it returns invalid via the relation_unsatisfied branch even when the executed output agrees with the relation's answer. Two-sided acceptance is therefore structurally capped at one half, and the cap is a property of the verifier rather than of the instrument — so the registered minimum of 0.5 is a ceiling the criterion could reach only by being vacuous, and a reader comparing the registered description to the run record would find the denominator halved. Acceptance on the satisfying half is the quantity that actually discriminates: an inverted model is rejected there — where a threshold-only check sees a model that is confidently wrong in the same direction on both halves — and a model that separates already passes criterion 2, so criterion 4 is the cross-check that the separation runs in the direction the benchmark's own verifier reads. The criterion's registered purpose, 'a gate that passes a model the task stream's own verifier rejects', is preserved by this reading and was never achievable by the two-sided one
amendments.discovered: by static inspection of src/tac_osm/structured_verifier.py:154, where a non-satisfying descriptor is rejected unconditionally, and confirmed by a torch-free probe of the implemented criterion against the three fake-runtime modes. Found before any confirmatory run; the implementation has always scored the satisfying half, and the amendment records what the code does rather than changing it
amendments.affected: the gate-table row for criterion 4 in docs/TACOSM-C5-003.md, whose 'registered constant' cell now names the half; the run record's verifier_acceptance entry, whose n_compared is the pair count rather than twice it; and the held_constant that describes the criterion. Criteria 1, 2 and 3, which read the same outputs, are unaffected, as are criteria 5-8, which are structural or constant-valued
amendments.no_result_under_previous_version: no confirmatory C5-003 run has been made under either definition. The two-sided reading has never been computed by the committed script, so no measured number exists to reconcile against the amendment; the --smoke run's criterion-4 value used the satisfying-half measure throughout and is smoke, not a measurement
